name: Tamazight Berber
catalog_quote: Word stress in Tamazight is a non-contrastive feature. The occurence of word stress is predictable: primary stress falls on the last vowel of the word. (Abdel-Massih 1971:17) [...] The above statement applies also to words that phonemically do not contain a vowel /V/. In these words stress is on the inserted schwa of the last syllable.

audit.recode_to: Drop 'fixed-strict final'. reclassify as weight-sensitive/unbounded with a lexical-class split (nouns: rightmost heavy syllable, else initial; verbs: final / rightmost full vowel) or, minimally, flag as 'contested — dialect- and category-dependent' with contra entries for Penchoen 1973:11 (no lexical stress, phrase-level right-edge prominence) and Faizi 2011:115-125 / Hdouch 2010 (weight-sensitive, default-initial nominal stress in Goulmima and Ait Wirra Tamazight); confirm against Hdouch 2010 and Faizi 2009 before finalising.
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim in the HathiTrust scan we hold of Abdel-Massih 1971 at book pp.17-18 (PDF pp.41-42); the StressTyp2 passage is a faithful paraphrase. (2) The deciding source is a 1971 reference grammar, but its stress paragraph is brief, impressionistic, and all of its examples are verbs. (3) Everything later and more specialised that I could open points away from 'strict fixed final' for Central Atlas Tamazight as a languoid: Penchoen 1973:11 (held; Ayt Ndhir) denies lexical stress and describes only phrase-level right-edge prominence; Faizi 2011 (downloaded, Asinag 6) and Faizi 2017 (downloaded, Asinag 12), summarising Faizi 2002/2009 on Goulmima Tamazight and Hdouch 2010 on Ait Wirra Tamazight, report weight-sensitive nominal stress with INITIAL default (61% of GA words initial-stressed, table p.121), final/rightmost-full-vowel stress only in verbs (which Faizi exp
audit.second_reader_evidence: The quotation was checked again: confirmed in the copy we hold. Rendered PDF pp.41-42 of (= book pp.17-18, §I.4 'Stress'): 'Word stress in Tamazight is a non-contrastive feature. The occurence of word stress is predictable: primary stress falls on the last vowel of the word (i.e. /V/ or [ə]).' p.18: 'The above statement applies to words that phonemically do not contain a vowel /V/.. In these cases, word primary stress is on the [ə] of the last syllable.' Verbatim match to sources[0].text; StressTyp2 the domain quotation is a faithful paraphrase. I confirm the other first reader's observation that every example is a verb form: p.17 /sál, ʕáwn, šk:á
